description: A tempo-driven function generator: it takes a 0-10V phasor or a clock and cuts one to sixteen envelopes out of every cycle of it, with controls that bend where in the cycle those envelopes fall

params.text: Reads the rate input as a 0-10V phasor while it is lit, following a change of rate at once; unlit, that input is read as a clock and two pulses are needed before a cycle length is known
Sets the attack of each envelope as a percentage of one hit's share of the cycle, 1 to 100 percent
Sets how far into each hit the envelope holds its full level, as a percentage of one hit's share of the cycle, 0 to 100 percent; that level is always the envelope's maximum
Sets how far into each hit the envelope reaches zero, as a percentage of one hit's share of the cycle, 1 to 100 percent
Bends the attack segment, 0 to 2: below 1 it rises fast and then slows, at 1 it is a straight line, above 1 it starts slowly. The display draws the envelope as though this were at 1
Bends the decay segment, 0 to 2: below 1 it falls fast and then slows, at 1 it is a straight line, above 1 it starts slowly. The display draws the envelope as though this were at 1
Sets how many envelopes are cut from each cycle, 1 to 16, or one of the other counts chosen from the menu
Sets where in the cycle the phase turns round, 0 to 1: at 1 it rises across the whole cycle, at 0.5 it rises over the first half and falls over the second, at 0 it falls across the whole cycle
Bends the phase before the envelopes are cut from it, so some envelopes are dwelt on and others passed through quickly; 1 is no bending, below 1 logarithmic and above 1 exponential
Reduces each envelope's height in proportion to how far through the cycle the phase has reached, from no reduction at 0 percent to complete at 100 percent

inputs.text: Takes the 0-10V phasor the envelopes are cut from, or a clock when the phase button is unlit
The signal multiplied by the envelope and sent to the vca output
Adds to the attack slider, 0-10V covering the whole of its travel
Adds to the sustain slider, 0-10V covering the whole of its travel
Adds to the decay slider, 0-10V covering the whole of its travel
Sets the number of hits in place of the knob while patched, 0-10V spread evenly over whichever counts the menu's hit count setting offers
Sets the turning point of the phase in place of the knob while patched, 0-10V giving 0 to 1
Sets the bending of the phase in place of the knob while patched, 0-10V giving 0 to 1, the lower half of the knob's own 0 to 2 travel
Scales how far the phase reduces the envelope's height, its 0-10V multiplied by the phase->env knob

outputs.text: The envelope, 0-10V, smoothed by a one-pole filter so that a sudden edge is rounded
The vca input multiplied by the envelope
Carries 10V through the whole attack segment of each envelope and for 1ms after it, rather than the short trigger at the start of the attack that the manual describes
The phase after skew and spread, 0-10V, which is the grey shape drawn on the display

notes: nothing comes out until a phasor or a clock is patched to rate: with that jack empty the phase stays at zero, the env output stays at 0V and the trig output stays high at 10V
the display is drawing only; no part of it responds to a click, and neither exp trimpot nor the phase->env knob is reflected in what it draws
the hit count and the rate input range chosen from the menu are not saved with the patch, so both return to their first setting when a patch is reloaded
menu: Hit Count — a heading over four settings for what the hits knob steps through
1-16 — the hits knob steps through every whole number from 1 to 16
1 and powers of two — the hits knob steps through 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16
evens — the hits knob steps through 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14, although its top position prints as 16
multiples of 3 — the hits knob steps through 3, 6, 9, 12 and 15
rate input range — a heading over the two readings of the rate input
unipolar (0-10v) — reads one cycle at the rate input as 0V rising to 10V
bipolar(-5-5v) — adds half a cycle to the rate input, so one cycle is -5V rising to 5V
